title: Implement allocator tuning + backpressure to mitigate cross-deployment GPU OOMs and memory corruption
creator: Priya Shah
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported spikes in GPU memory usage culminating in node-level OOMs and sporadic KV cache corruption. Early signals indicate allocator memory fragmentation combined with delayed KV cache eviction under high-concurrency workloads; a few Private deployments also surfaced a stale pointer bug in the cache eviction path. This ticket tracks investigation, immediate mitigations (hotfixes and operational playbook), and a runtime allocator change + proactive backpressure controls to prevent recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotfix and canary deploy reduce observed OOM incidents to near-zero for affected customers for 48h. 2) Runtime allocator patch merged and passes perf/regression tests (<=5% median token latency change, >=15% GPU memory reduction under synthetic workload). 3) Backpressure/eviction knobs available via config and documented in Console. 4) Postmortem published with root cause, customer impact timeline, and long-term mitigations (per-tenant memory quotas, stronger KV cache invariants).
comments: 2026-02-16 — SEV2 received from Acme Games (dedicated) and two hosted customers: reproducible GPU OOMs during 8k token streaming requests. Initial triage by on-call indicates heavy KV cache growth preceding OOMs.

2026-02-18 — Assigned to Liam O'Connor. Initial hypothesis: combination of allocator fragmentation + long-lived KV cache entries (large embeddings) that avoid eviction due to stale LRU metadata under concurrency.

2026-02-19 — Reproduced locally with stress harness (model: redwood-v2-13b, sequence=8k, batch=6). Observed memory climb with no immediate free activity; heap snapshots show many small free fragments and inflated arena metadata.

2026-02-21 — Operational mitigation deployed (PR #4589): reduce default KV cache TTL for streaming paths from 15m to 5m, enable CPU offload for oversized keys, and add a script to gracefully restart affected nodes. Notified customers and provisioned short-term extra capacity for impacted Dedicated pools.

2026-02-24 — Found a code path in eviction logic where under heavy concurrency a race allows an entry to be marked live while being evicted; this left stale pointers in KV index on some Private deployments where strict ASAN-like checks were enabled. Filed internal bug note and added assertion checks in debug builds.

2026-02-26 — Prototype allocator change: bucketed slab allocator with proactive compaction intervals. Microbenchmarks show ~18% lower peak GPU memory for synthetic streaming workload but a small median token latency increase (~1.8%). Opened PR #4621 for review.

2026-03-02 — Canary rollout of PL (hotfix + KV TTL change) to 10% of Hosted capacity and 1 Dedicated customer. After 72h, observed 60% reduction in OOM frequency and no recurrence of KV corruption on canary nodes.

2026-03-04 — Security and correctness review notes: add additional invariants to eviction path, enable extra logging at info level for 7 days, and add a runtime flag to force synchronous compaction during low-load windows. Reviewed by Security (Anya Morales) and Applied ML (Dr. Wei Zhang).

2026-03-06 — Merged PR #4621 (allocator) after addressing reviewer concerns about fragmentation thresholds and benchmarking on A100 and H100. Backported critical assertion fixes to runtime-1.18 branch for affected Private customers on older releases.

2026-03-08 — QA run against regression suite: token throughput unchanged within noise, p50 latency +2.2% on H100 workloads at low concurrency, peak GPU mem down ~22% on synthetic streams. Decision: proceed with staged rollout to Dedicated pools under maintenance windows.

2026-03-09 — Plan for rollout: 1) Patch Dedicated pools in maintenance window (2026-03-12) with automated validation checks, 2) Offer Private customers the backport package and operator guidance, 3) Add per-tenant memory quota feature as follow-up (ENG-13790).

2026-03-10 — PM update (Rashida Kumar): coordinate customer communications and billing adjustments for the short-term extra capacity. Request for full postmortem and customer-facing summary within 5 business days after rollout completes.
